name: Windows Endpoint Hunt
author: Red Cell Team
prerequisites: Sysmon deployed with baseline config (SwiftOnSecurity recommended)
EDR telemetry available and actively collecting
Remote access via WinRM or EDR console
required_tools: Splunk or Elastic with Windows Event Log index

hunt_actions.title: Malicious PowerShell Execution
actions: Hunt for PowerShell spawned by Office applications: Windows Event 4688 or Sysmon Event 1. Splunk: `index=windows (EventCode=4688 OR EventCode=1) ParentImage IN (*WINWORD.EXE*,*EXCEL.EXE*,*OUTLOOK.EXE*) Image=*powershell* | table _time, host, ParentImage, Image, CommandLine`

Detect encoded command-line executions: `index=windows EventCode=4688 CommandLine=*-EncodedCommand* OR CommandLine=*-enc* | rex field=CommandLine '-[Ee][Nn][Cc][Oo]?[Dd]?[Ee]?[Dd]? (?P<encoded>[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+)' | eval decoded=base64decode(encoded) | table _time, host, decoded` — decode and inspect for IEX, Net.WebClient, or download cradles.

Identify PowerShell downloading from internet: Windows PowerShell ScriptBlock log (Event 4104). Splunk: `index=windows EventCode=4104 (ScriptBlockText=*DownloadString* OR ScriptBlockText=*IEX* OR ScriptBlockText=*Invoke-Expression* OR ScriptBlockText=*WebClient*) | table _time, host, ScriptBlockText`

Hunt for AMSI bypass strings: `index=windows EventCode=4104 (ScriptBlockText=*amsiInitFailed* OR ScriptBlockText=*AmsiScanBuffer* OR ScriptBlockText=*amsiContext* OR ScriptBlockText=*Reflection.Assembly*) | table _time, host, Path, ScriptBlockText`

hunt_actions.title: Persistence via Registry and Scheduled Tasks
actions: Review Run/RunOnce keys for unsigned binaries: Sysmon Event 13 (RegistryValueSet). Splunk: `index=windows EventCode=13 TargetObject IN (*\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run*,*\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce*) | table _time, host, TargetObject, Details` — then validate each binary path with `Get-AuthenticodeSignature <path>`.

Audit scheduled tasks created in last 30 days: On endpoint run `schtasks /query /fo CSV /v | ConvertFrom-Csv | Where-Object { $_.Status -ne 'Disabled' -and $_.'Run As User' -eq 'SYSTEM' } | Select TaskName, 'Task To Run', 'Run As User'` or Velociraptor: `SELECT * FROM Artifact.Windows.System.ScheduledTasks() WHERE Principal.UserId = 'S-1-5-18'`

Hunt WMI event subscriptions: `Get-WMIObject -Namespace root\subscription -Class __EventFilter | Select Name, Query` and `Get-WMIObject -Namespace root\subscription -Class CommandLineEventConsumer | Select Name, CommandLineTemplate` — any result is suspicious unless tied to known software (AV/EDR).

Detect services installed outside deployment windows: Windows Event 7045 (new service installed). Splunk: `index=windows EventCode=7045 | eval day_of_week=strftime(_time,'%A') | where day_of_week!='Tuesday' AND day_of_week!='Wednesday' | table _time, host, ServiceName, ImagePath, AccountName` — adjust patch window days to match your environment.

hunt_actions.title: Process Injection Indicators
actions: Hunt for unusual parent-child process relationships: Sysmon Event 1. Splunk: `index=windows EventCode=1 (ParentImage=*winword.exe* OR ParentImage=*excel.exe*) Image IN (*cmd.exe*,*powershell.exe*,*wscript.exe*,*cscript.exe*,*mshta.exe*,*regsvr32.exe*) | table _time, host, ParentImage, Image, CommandLine`

Detect CreateRemoteThread (DLL injection): Sysmon Event 8. Splunk: `index=windows EventCode=8 TargetImage!=*svchost.exe* | table _time, host, SourceImage, TargetImage, StartAddress, StartModule` — review any SourceImage that does not normally inject (non-AV/EDR processes).

Identify processes with unexpected network connections: Sysmon Event 3 (Network Connect). Splunk: `index=windows EventCode=3 Image IN (*notepad.exe*,*calc.exe*,*mspaint.exe*,*wordpad.exe*) | table _time, host, Image, DestinationIp, DestinationPort` — static apps should never initiate outbound connections.

questions: Is Sysmon deployed on all endpoints with a hardened configuration (e.g., SwiftOnSecurity or Olaf Hartong Modular Config), and what is the current config version/hash?
Which EDR platform is deployed, and is it operating in active prevention mode or detection-only (audit) mode across all endpoint populations?
Is PowerShell ScriptBlock logging (Event 4104) and Module logging (Event 4103) enabled organization-wide via Group Policy, and are these logs forwarded to the SIEM?
Are Windows Defender or third-party AV exclusions formally documented, approved by a security authority, and reviewed at least quarterly for scope creep?
What is the current endpoint patch compliance rate, and what percentage of endpoints are within 30 days of the latest OS and third-party application security patches?
Is Windows Event Log forwarding (WEF) or an EDR agent configured to centrally ship Security, System, and Application event logs to a SIEM, and what is the maximum ingest lag?
Are privileged administrative accounts (local admin, domain admin) separated from day-to-day user accounts, and is there a Privileged Access Workstation (PAW) or jump server policy in place?

Is LSA Protection (RunAsPPL) or Windows Credential Guard enabled to prevent LSASS memory dumping, and has this been verified via `Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa -Name RunAsPPL`?
